subject: Link: Discrete uniform priors for binomial N

messages.author: 2a3a0c6a456f3043
messages.subject: Link: Discrete uniform priors for binomial N
parts:
Hi all,

This might not be the appropriate place to ask a question about primarily Bayesian inference since unmarked takes a MLE approach, but my question is in regards to the binomial mixture model. I don't know where else I'd find an answer to this, so any thoughts would be appreciated.

Bill Link just published a research note in Ecology cautioning the against the use of uniform priors for binomial N when using models such as the N-mixture model. http://www.esajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1890/13-0176.1

The paper is a bit over my head and I'm going to have to read it another time or two, but I think I followed the general idea. However, I always include covariates on log(lambda) and logit(p) so I have priors on the coefficients of those covariates but not explicitly on N or p (using WinBUGS or JAGS). I am wondering how the ideas presented in this paper might apply to this situation? Does anyone actually go through and check if all the posteriors are proper in these situations? Is it sufficient in pratical cases to just visually examine the posterior distributions and look to make sure that they differ from the priors and that the distribution looks good?

Thanks for any thoughts,
Dan

Best,
